s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive imbalance and vertigo with chronic periventricular white matter changes
salient_findings: Recurrent dizzying attacks with sudden subjective vertigo
key_facts: 75-year-old woman
Presumed stroke in April 2020
Slurred speech, imbalance, and confusion lasting 48 hours
Brain MRI showed chronic periventricular white matter changes
CT angiography demonstrated carotid tortuosity with stenosis
Medications included barnidipine, clopidogrel, and atorvastatin
Recurrent dizzying attacks increased in frequency and duration
Normal general and neurologic examinations at first visit
Low mood reported
Severe dizziness worsened by movement or position change
Normal vital signs
Normal speech
Difficulty maintaining trunk control
Wide-based stance and unsteadiness when upright
Normal strength and sensation
Normal reflexes and cranial nerves
Weakly positive finger-nose test on the right
Negative HINTS examination

shortlist.label: Multiple System Atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive imbalance and vertigo with autonomic dysfunction

shortlist.label: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 6
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic progressive ataxia with imbalance and vertigo

shortlist.label: Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus
shortlist.why_kept: Gait disturbance and imbalance with chronic periventricular white matter changes

shortlist.label: Cerebellar Atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic progressive ataxia with imbalance and vertigo

shortlist.label: CADASIL
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic periventricular white matter changes with recurrent episodes of imbalance and vertigo

raw.rationale: The patient's progressive and recurrent dizzying attacks, difficulty with balance and trunk control, wide-based stance, and unsteadiness are consistent with the symptoms of Multiple System Atrophy, which is a neurodegenerative disorder that affects balance, movement, and the autonomic nervous system.

rejected.label: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 6
rejected.why: While it could explain some of the balance issues, the overall clinical presentation and progression do not fully align with the typical symptoms of Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 6.

rejected.label: Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the classic triad of gait disturbance, dementia, and urinary incontinence typically seen in Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus.

rejected.label: Cerebellar Atrophy
rejected.why: Cerebellar Atrophy could explain some of the balance issues, but it does not account for the full spectrum of the patient's symptoms, including the progression and severity of the condition.

rejected.label: CADASIL
rejected.why: CADASIL typically presents with migraine headaches, strokes, and dementia, which are not prominent features in this patient's presentation.
